title: split-proxy-paths-nlb-sni-preserve-session-terraform
creator: Asha Raman
description: Refactor the internal ingress Terraform module to split proxy paths so that NLB handles TCP passthrough and SNI-preservation while ALB performs TLS termination for HTTP traffic. This will allow us to (1) preserve client IP and SNI for legacy TCP services, (2) centralize TLS termination and header enrichment on ALB for web workloads, and (3) support safe, weighted canary rollouts with health-check-aware traffic shifting. The module must support blue/green and gradual traffic shifting, Proxy Protocol v2, connection draining, configurable health probe strategies (HTTP/gRPC/TCP), and zero-downtime certificate rotation using ACM/Secrets manager hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes variables to enable/disable NLB passthrough and ALB termination per service
Ingress stacks can perform a weighted rollout (0-100%) to new target groups with no 5xx spike observed in synthetic tests
SNI and client source IP are preserved for TCP passthrough listeners and visible to backend targets
ACM certificate rotation triggers automated rebinds in ALB with health-check gating and no connection loss for HTTP clients
Health checks can be switched between HTTP, gRPC, and TCP per-service without changing module interface
Module includes automated Terraform plan guardrails and prevents destructive changes to production target groups unless 'force_apply' is explicitly set
design_notes: Architecture: NLB in front for L4 TCP passthrough (preserve SNI, ProxyProtocol v2 option) -> optional ALB for L7 TLS termination and routing
We will add a 'proxy_mode' var: values {passthrough, terminate, split}. 'split' creates parallel NLB and ALB paths and a Route controller that maps services to one or the other via tags
Session stickiness: support both cookie-based ALB stickiness and NLB source-ip affinity (by enabling target group 'preserve_client_ip')
TLS: ALB uses ACM certificates; for private ACMS we store ARN in state and provide rotation hooks that sequence: provision new cert, attach to ALB, wait for healthy targets, then remove old cert
Canary: use ALB target group weights with AWS Lambda-based traffic-shift helper for precise splits where necessary
Health probes: default path '/_hc/ingress' returns 200 with JSON {status:ok} and includes probe hints for backends to bypass expensive startup checks
Metrics: emit per-target-group latency/5xx and probe-failure counters to CloudWatch; add alert thresholds to SLO playbook
terraform_changes: Variables: proxy_mode (string), enable_proxy_protocol (bool), canary_weight (number), health_check_type (string), certificate_arn (string), stickiness_mode (string), deregistration_delay (number)

Resources: aws_lb (ALB), aws_lb_listener + aws_lb_listener_rule, aws_lb_target_group, aws_lb_target_group_attachment, aws_lb (NLB), aws_lb_listener for TCP passthrough, aws_lb_target_group for NLB (IP mode), aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm for probe failures
Outputs: alb_arn, nlb_arn, primary_target_group_id, canary_target_group_id, listener_map (list of listener ARNs)
Lifecycle: use 'create_before_destroy' for target groups and listeners; add 'prevent_destroy' toggle controlled by 'allow_destructive' variable
State migration: provide a 'state_migration.tf' example to map old module outputs to new module inputs for teams upgrading
migration_plan: 1) Create parallel staging ingress stack in the same VPC with module v2 and route 0% traffic to it
2) Smoke test staging with synthetic gRPC/HTTP/TCP probes and confirm metrics/headers and client IP preservation
3) Perform a 5% canary shift to staging target group for a low-traffic service and monitor for 15 minutes
4) Increment weights (25%, 50%, 75%) observing latency/5xx and taking automated rollback if error_rate > 0.5%
5) Once at 100%, decommission legacy target group using terraform with 'plan' review and scheduled maintenance window
6) For cert rotation: provision new ACM cert, attach to ALB with canary weight 1%, verify health, then promote
7) Coordinate with network/security to enable Proxy Protocol v2 where NLB passthrough is used (agents on host OS must support v2 headers)
testing_plan: Unit: terraform validate and terratest for module inputs/outputs and lifecycle behaviors
Integration: deploy to staging VPC, run synthetic HTTP/gRPC/TCP probes including long-lived connections to validate idle timeout handling
Load test: k6 scenario that ramps to 3x normal QPS with sudden connection churn to validate deregistration_delay and connection draining
Chaos: simulate node termination and AZ failover to ensure ALB/NLB fallback policies and cross-zone balancing behave as expected
Security: pen test for TLS renegotiation and SNI spoofing on passthrough listeners
Canary observability: dashboards should show target-group weight, probe success rate, 95/99p latency, and backend error traces
rollback_plan: If canary shows >0.5% 5xx or latency >2x baseline, immediately shift traffic back to previous target group weights via the weighted-targets Lambda runbook
Use Terraform plan only to make state changes; avoid direct console changes unless emergency, and record them in an incident ticket
If ALB cert attach causes failures, detach new cert and reattach old cert, then revert terraform apply for listener change
In extreme cases, switch DNS entry to point to legacy NLB/ALB pair using TTL 30s and failover script
